title: Finding a work order by its customer's name still works
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in with access to Work Orders.
2. A customer named "Peterson Freight" has at least one work order.
custom_steps:
1. Open global search.
2. Type the customer's name: Peterson
3. Look at the Work Orders group in the results.
custom_expected:
1. The customer's work orders are listed under the Work Orders group.
2. You do not have to know the work order number to find them.

Based on the Global Search V2 PRD v1.2 (Confluence version 12), which is SILENT on this behaviour, so Standing Rule 96 keeps the V1 behaviour as an invariant that must not change. V1 behaviour established from the ShopView code baseline 55767168 (FetchDataQueryHandler.php:91-118 - the work order search text includes the customer name). Not yet checked against any V2 build - no Global Search QA build exists.

title: A work order number with the shop number in front still finds it

   b. S1234

   d. 12-1234

title: The search box shows a loading state until results are ready
custom_preconds: 1. You are signed in with any role that can use global search.
custom_steps:
1. Sign in and go straight to any page with the header search box.
2. Watch the search box while the page finishes loading.
custom_expected:
1. Until search is ready the box is not typeable and shows a loading indication.
2. Once ready it becomes typeable and shows the normal Search prompt.
3. Typing is never silently ignored.

Based on the Global Search V2 PRD v1.2 (Confluence version 12), which is SILENT on this behaviour, so Standing Rule 96 keeps the V1 behaviour as an invariant that must not change. V1 behaviour established from the ShopView code baseline 55767168 (GlobalSearch.vue:12-14 and 147-149 - the input was disabled and showed Loading... until the search data had loaded). Not yet checked against any V2 build - no Global Search QA build exists.
